page: Amazon Web Services r8in.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. Driven by 3.9 GHz dedicated Intel x86_64 processors, the instance delivers 64 vCPUs distributed across 32 physical cores with 2 threads per core. It is configured with 512.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU allocation ratio of 8.0 GB per core to handle memory-intensive compute environments.

Network connectivity is a focal hardware metric for the r8in.16xlarge, providing a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps. The instance contains no integrated GPUs and includes no local instance storage. As a result, all disk persistence and stateful storage operations require external attachment via Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) or network file systems, routing I/O through its network interface.

Hardware allocation is dedicated to the virtual machine, eliminating core oversubscription and stabilizing multi-threaded execution. With high memory density per core and 100 Gbps networking, the instance offers balanced resource utilization for scenarios limited by RAM capacity and data transfer speeds rather than localized storage latency. The platform is well suited for enterprise in-memory databases, large caching clusters, distributed data analysis, and memory-bound ETL workflows.
description: Amazon Web Services r8in.16xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine operating on the AWS Nitro System. Driven by dedicated Intel processors running at 3.9 GHz, it features 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores alongside 512.0 GB of RAM, sustaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Designed for high-throughput network environments, the instance offers a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps to support intensive cluster communication and distributed processing. There is no bundled local storage or GPU hardware, requiring workloads to rely on remote storage solutions such as Amazon EBS for persistence. This configuration delivers an efficient footprint for workloads constrained by memory capacity and network throughput rather than local disk speed. Consequently, r8in.16xlarge is suited for in-memory databases, large-scale distributed caching services, real-time telemetry processing, and large in-memory data transformation pipelines.
